messages:
Marie (AE): Quick heads-up — BridgeCorp wants a focused latency & throughput run tomorrow 10:00am PT. Finalizing runbook and a short pricing note for reserved vs burst capacity. Can we confirm owners?
Liam (SE): I can own the test plan + metrics. Will need test data shape and target QPS from BridgeCorp.
BridgeCorp POC: Thanks — aiming for sustained 120 QPS for chat completions (avg prompt ~120 tokens, gen ~80 tokens). 99th pct latency target <250ms. We also want a 5-min spike to 400 QPS for resilience.
Jess (DevEx): Noted. For token math: at 200 tokens/req that's ~24k tokens/sec sustained. Will want to validate token billing estimates for the prospect afterward.
Anika (Sales-Eng): Also confirm if they need dedicated capacity pricing. They've asked about a committed plan estimate for 6 months.
Devon (SRE): I'll coordinate infra (test harness + traffic shaping). Suggest we use k6 for sustained QPS and a short vegeta burst test.
Liam (SE): Proposed run steps (short):
- Warmup 10m at 30% QPS
- Ramp to 100% over 5m
- Sustained 60m at 120 QPS (collect p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, error rate)
- Spike test: ramp to 400 QPS for 5m, then immediate fall back to 120 QPS
- Repeat with prefix/KV cache enabled vs disabled

Liam (SE): k6 script snippet we'll use:
```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = { vus: 200, duration: '1h', rps: 120 };
export default function () {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({ prompt: '<<redacted-test-prompt>>', max_tokens: 80 });
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer TEST_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
  sleep(0.1);
}
```
Jess (DevEx): We'll run against a dedicated test model variant (quantized) and the full-precision for comparison. I can deploy a small Canary pool in us-west-2.
BridgeCorp POC: Can you also confirm data residency? Their compliance team requires logs to stay in US only.
Devon (SRE): Use region=us-west-2 for all traffic. We'll mask customer content in logs; send sec questionnaire answers after the run.
Anika (Sales-Eng): Pricing note for AE deck: If they commit to reserved capacity (3x 8-GPU nodes) we can offer 20% discount and a 99.9% uptime SLA. For short-term POC they can use burst credits on hosted API — we should show delta cost for sustained 120 QPS vs reserved.
Liam (SE): I'll capture per-token cost estimates: rough calc
- Hosted (no commit): $0.0008 / token (example) -> sustained run cost ~= $0.0008 * 24k * 3600 * 1 = $69,120 per hour (obviously we will put accurate model per-token)
- Dedicated reserved (amortized): estimate ~$X/hr for reserved 8-GPU pool -> much lower per-token.
Marie (AE): OK please put numbers in a one-pager after the run. BridgeCorp buying committee wants clear ops + cost case.
Liam (SE): After test we'll produce short results summary: p50/p95/p99, token/sec, successful req/s, error %; screenshots of Console traces and per-route cost.
Devon (SRE): Quick infra checklist:
- Test key scoped to BridgeCorp POC tenant
- Region pinned to us-west-2
- Canary pool: 3 nodes (auto-scaling off)
- Logging retention set to 7d for POC
- Alert rule: error rate >1% -> stop test

Jess (DevEx): I'll also prepare a Canary dashboard: token/sec, avg latency, 99th, GPU utilization, queue depth.
BridgeCorp POC: Great — one ask: can you also show KV/prefix cache impact? Their app heavily reuses context.
Liam (SE): Yes we'll run with cache off, then cache on (same workload) and capture latency + token cost delta.
Anika (Sales-Eng): Who owns the security questionnaire follow-up? I can handle the SOC2 / encryption Qs with security team.
Devon (SRE): Devon will drop answers into the questionnaire doc. @Anika I'll ping you when it's staged.
Marie (AE): Logistics: test tomorrow 10:00am PT. Meet in #sales-bridgecorp-run at 9:45 for pre-check. Who can be on the call?
Liam (SE): I'll be on call.
Jess (DevEx): I'll join for dashboard walkthrough.
Devon (SRE): On standby for infra.
Anika (Sales-Eng): I'll join for pricing & contractual clarifications.
BridgeCorp POC: We'll have engineering and procurement on the call. Thanks.
Liam (SE) (later): Quick post-run summary (results):
- Sustained 120 QPS run (60m): avg latency 158ms, p95 240ms, p99 390ms, success rate 99.6%, token/sec observed 23,900
- Spike to 400 QPS: error rate peaked at 2.3% during first 45s, then autoscaling/fallback kicked in; tail latencies hit p99 1.8s during spike
- Cache on vs off: cache ON reduced avg latency by ~42% and cut token compute by ~35% (approx)
- Console traces: a handful of 502s during peak — root cause was queue saturation on one node, mitigated by fallback routing to reserved pool

Liam (SE): Attached (in thread) are: concise CSV of metrics, screenshot of dashboard, and a short cost comparison table.
Marie (AE): Perfect — please convert to 1-slide summary for the exec committee and a 2-page technical appendix.
Anika (Sales-Eng): I'll draft the committed pricing options and include the POC hourly numbers vs reserved amortized.
BridgeCorp POC: This is helpful. Next steps from our side: internal review, security sign-off, and procurement wants a formal quote for 6-month reserved capacity.
Marie (AE): We'll aim to deliver the quote + SOC2 appendix by EOD Friday. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
